newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BARCELONA TRAVEL IN HOPE OF IMPROVING FINISHING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA TRAVEL IN HOPE OF IMPROVING FINISHING.

text.p: The Cup Winners' Cup, often a consolation for former European champions after a dip in their domestic league fortunes, should see Barcelona, Benfica, PSV Eindhoven and Liverpool progress after the first round second legs on Thursday.

Three times winners Barcelona, one of only four sides to have won all three European club competitions, believe they can score more goals away against lightweight AEK Larnaca of Cyprus after a paltry 2-0 home win two weeks ago.
"We musn't lose this game. The first goal will be very important... In the first leg we should have scored four or five goals and I think we'll do that there," said coach Bobby Robson.

Barcelona are without injured Spain international midfielder Josep Guardiola, striker Juan Pizzi and defender Sergi Barjuan, but the strength in depth of their multi-billion peseta squad means the absences will hardly be noticed.
Brazil's Ronaldo, signed from PSV in the off-season, scored both goals in the home leg.

Liverpool will be wary of the tenacity of their Finnish rivals MyPa-47 Anjalonkoski after being limited to a 1-0 away win, but the English premier league leaders, 5-1 winners over Chelsea on Saturday, should coast through at home.
Benfica visit Ruch Chorzow of Poland with a 5-1 lead from the first leg, while PSV are level at 1-1 with Dynamo Batumi of Georgia going into their home leg.
A fifth former European Cup-winning team, Red Star Belgrade are 1-0 down, but home advantage in front of a crowd expected to be near 100,000 could help them through against Kaiserslautern.

The Germans, relegated in their cup winning season, still have two key players of Euro 96 runners-up the Czech Republic, striker Pavel Kuka and Miroslav Kadlec, but the defender is one several injury doubts for coach Otto Rehhagel.
Former Germany defender Andreas Brehme stands by in case Kadlec fails a late fitness test.
Kaiserslautern are bidding to become the first German second division side to reach the second round in European competition.
Nimes look set to become the first French third division side to progress beyond the first round in Europe as they defend a 3-1 lead away to Hungarians Kispest Honved.
France have two clubs in the Cup Winners' Cup with holders Paris Saint-Germain at home to Vaduz with a 4-0 lead from the first leg.

The Liechtenstein part-timers' only hope of scoring against a PSG side that has yet to concede a goal under Ricardo this season is if the Brazilian manager tests a few inexperienced players in a tie virtually sewn up two weeks ago.
Goalkeeper Bernard Lama is out injured, while Ricardo may rest Lama's fellow French internationals defender Alain Roche and midfielder Vincent Guerin.
Gabriel Batistuta's Fiorentina are level at 1-1 ahead of the home leg against Gloria Bistrita of Romania thanks to the Argentine striker's away equaliser.

Sparta Prague, taking part for the sixth time, have two away goals from a first leg 2-2 draw with Sturm Graz of Austria going into the home leg, but coach Jozef Chovanec has warned his team against complacency.
"We have the chance to move to the second round in our hands and we can't let it slip out with a defensive mistake. We can't let down our guard even for a second," he said.
Chemlon Humenne of neighbouring Slovakia, playing in Europe for the first time, are 1-0 down against AEK Athens despite dominating much of the away leg.
"In Athens we put up a fight and attacked constantly, though we could not get the equaliser. On Thursday we will do the same," vowed coach Ondrej Danko.
Away goals could also stand Brann Bergen of Norway in good stead when they face Cercle Brugge of Belgium 3-2 down.
In Fiorentina, Brazilian Luis Barroso Oliveira and Italian striker Anselmo Robbiati will line up alongside Batistuta, nicknamed Batigol in Italy.
The same trio led Fiorentina to a 2-0 win over Verona on Sunday -- their first league victory of the season.
"A three-pronged attack can go well both both for home and away games," Fiorentina coach Claudio Ranieri said.

"But we're cautious...everyone thinks we're already through to the next round and are only talking about our league game next Sunday against Juventus. But the truth is Gloria Bistrita are a dangerous team."
Portugal's Manuel Cesar Rui Costa is expected to play behind the front three, in the role of play maker.
Kispest Honved play at their Bozsik stadium, named after a team mate of the great Ferenc Puskas.

They will need plenty of inspiration against Nimes but enter the tie in optimistic mood after a 2-1 away win at the weekend when Mihaly Toth, scorer of two of their three goals in the Cup Winners' Cup this season, hit the winner.
Toth, whose away goal at Nimes may prove useful, plays on Thursday in what is expected to be an unchanged team.
